Definition: lightning; by analogy, a gleam; concretely, a flashing sword
BiblicalUsage: Baraq is lightning, the flash and the gleam of a drawn sword. Thunders and lightnings attend the Lord's descent on Sinai, God says His glittering sword will take hold on judgment, Ezekiel sees the sword sharpened to flash like lightning, and the psalm asks God to cast forth lightning and scatter His enemies.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe lightning is Scripture's picture of a God who cannot be managed, because it comes when He sends it and strikes where He wills. The same flash that lit Sinai still warns us, and I hold that the God of the lightning is the God whose sword is never drawn for nothing.
